\subsection*{Randomized --- BPPAmplify: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity in the acceptance threshold]
\lean{Randomized.BPP_PTMWith_mono}
\label{Randomized.BPP_PTMWith_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPP_PTMWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p,q:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $q(n)\leq p(n)$ for every $n$. Every language
decidable in polynomial time by a randomized machine whose probability of producing the
correct answer on inputs of length $n$ is at least $p(n)$ is also decidable in
polynomial time with that probability at least $q(n)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weak-error and length-dependent BPP coincide]
\lean{Randomized.inBPPWith_iff_inBPPWeak}
\label{Randomized.inBPPWith_iff_inBPPWeak}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InBPPWeak, Randomized.InBPPWith, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.weakAdv}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ be a natural number and let $L$ be a language of bit strings. The language $L$
has a polynomial-time verifier whose probability of the correct answer on inputs of
length $n$ is at least $1/2+\min\{1/6,(n+1)^{-c}\}$ if and only if it has a
polynomial-time verifier with that same success-probability bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strong-error and length-dependent BPP coincide]
\lean{Randomized.inBPPWith_iff_inBPPStrong}
\label{Randomized.inBPPWith_iff_inBPPStrong}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InBPPStrong, Randomized.InBPPWith, Randomized.polyTimeModel}
\difficulty{1}
Let $d$ be a natural number and let $L$ be a language of bit strings. The language $L$
has a polynomial-time verifier whose probability of the correct answer on inputs of
length $n$ is at least $1-(1/2)^{(n+1)^d+1}$ if and only if it has a polynomial-time
verifier with that same length-dependent success-probability bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Error reduction for randomized polynomial time]
\lean{Randomized.BPP_PTMWith_error_reduction}
\proofsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p025-b008}
\label{Randomized.BPP_PTMWith_error_reduction}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPP_PTMWith, Randomized.bpp_error_reduction_polyTime, Randomized.mem_BPP_PTMWith_iff, Randomized.weakAdv}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $c,d$, every language having a polynomial-time randomized
decider whose probability of producing the correct answer on inputs of length $n$ is at
least $1/2+\min\{1/6,(n+1)^{-c}\}$ also has a polynomial-time randomized decider whose
probability of producing the correct answer on inputs of length $n$ is at least
$1-(1/2)^{(n+1)^d+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[An Exponential Bound on a Power]
\lean{Randomized.exists_majority_count}
\label{Randomized.exists_majority_count}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For rational numbers $\varepsilon,\eta$ with $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$ and $\eta>0$, there
is a nonnegative integer $K$ such that $2(1-4\varepsilon^2)^{\lfloor
K/2\rfloor}\le\eta$.
\end{theorem}
